page: OVHcloud rtx5000-56 is a GPU-accelerated server configured with an Intel Xeon W-3235 processor featuring eight dedicated physical cores on the x86_64 architecture. Operating at a base clock speed of 3.3 GHz, the CPU includes 16 MB of L3 cache and supports AVX-512 vector extensions. The system is equipped with 56 GB of system memory, providing 7 GB per core. Acceleration is delivered via two NVIDIA Quadro RTX 5000 GPUs based on the Turing architecture, offering a combined total of 32 GB of VRAM. Local storage consists of a 400 GB SSD, and network connectivity is supported by a 4 Gbps baseline bandwidth under a KVM hypervisor.

Benchmark results indicate strong performance in memory operations, with a Passmark memory score categorized in the top 25% and a read-only small block memory bandwidth of 726.2 GB/sec. CPU performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core metrics falling into average ranges. The server demonstrates exceptional capabilities in low-parameter large language model inference, achieving top-tier results for both prompt processing and text generation on 135M and 7B models. However, memory write bandwidth for large blocks is relatively weak at 19.55 GB/sec, and single-threaded gzip compression also registers in the lower performance tier.

From a resource density perspective, the inclusion of dual dedicated GPUs alongside dedicated CPU cores offers a balanced hardware profile for parallel processing tasks without the overhead of larger multi-socket configurations. This makes the server highly suitable for GPU-accelerated workloads such as small-to-medium LLM inference, machine learning model training, and parallelized data processing. It is also well-suited for tasks requiring moderate host memory and dedicated CPU execution, though workloads heavily reliant on high-speed sequential memory writes may experience bottlenecks.
